source.title: Toward Mechanistic Interpretability of an AI Foundation Model Fine-Tuned for Atmospheric Chemistry
source.authors: Jason Hu; Iván Higuera-Mendieta; Patrick Obin Sturm; Makoto M. Kelp

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies atmospheric chemistry forecasts and SAE features in Aurora, not neuron-level job shares or the neuron-explanation tests in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports chemical perturbation, plume, and latent-structure findings, but these do not measure neuron job shares or test the listed versions. The SAE ablations are included as related internal-feature findings; they concern SAE features, not neurons.
record.test_reason: The paper studies Aurora, an atmospheric-chemistry forecasting model, using perturbations, PCA and SAE features. It reports no neuron-level job shares, no neuron explanations scored on held-out activations, no InceptionV1 analysis and no neuron-based attribution graphs. So it neither tests nor uses any version. The interpretability methods (SAEs, circuits) are only cited as background, so 'cites_only' fits better than 'discusses'.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also conclude that Aurora captures first-order NOx-ozone titration but violates positivity and chemical consistency, and that it smooths wildfire plumes. Its latent organization reflects inherited meteorology and architectural artifacts more than chemistry. SAE features causally affect forecasts but are chemically entangled, and the authors call for tests against process reference fields.
record.recipe_differences: The paper applies sparse autoencoders and feature ablation to an atmospheric foundation model; it does not use the neuron-pole audit or held-out neuron-explanation tests described in the claim.

fits_no_version.finding: Zero-ablating top SAE features in Aurora changes ozone and NO2 forecasts causally, but the effects are entangled across species. Some features are spatial artifacts, such as a single latitude band.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In an Earth-system foundation model, high-variance SAE features are causally active but do not map cleanly onto single physical processes.

record.problems: The paper reports two SAE-ablation case studies selected from the top ten features; it does not report uncertainty estimates for these effects. The authors also say the induced feature effects are entangled and difficult to interpret mechanistically.
record.rows_left_out: Chemical perturbation responses, wildfire plume persistence, PCA structure, and SAE reconstruction quality were not entered as rows because they do not measure the neuron-level constructs or tests in the claim versions.

untested.parts: All: neuron job shares across language models and scales.
All: interpretable-neuron share versus architecture and tools.
All: neuron-based attribution graphs versus replacement models.
All: whether activating-example explanations predict held-out firing.

record.verdict_notes: An atmospheric-science paper unrelated to neuron interpretability shares. The SAE features are dictionary features, not neurons, and the rows were chosen as the top-ten features by variance contribution. None of the rows bears on any version.

versions.untested_parts: Neuron job shares across models, architectures, and scales.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example and recursive generalization.
Neuron interpretability rates in vision models and their dependence on architecture, regularization, or tools.
Attribution graphs using a large model's own neurons, and comparison with replacement models or reconstruction error.
Whether explanations fitted to activating examples predict held-out activations.
Automated explanation scores from simulating neuron activations on new text.

rows.note: The result establishes a causal effect of an SAE feature on the forecast, but does not measure whether a neuron has one main job.
